name: SNAP (food assistance)
administeredBy: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration, through state agencies
valueBasis: Maximum allotment for the household size, less 30% of net monthly income, times twelve.

criteria.instructions: Does every member of this household receive one of these benefits? Answer 'none' unless the description indicates that all members receive the same one.
criteria.askIfUnsure: Does everyone in your household get SSI, TANF, or General Assistance?

criteria.none: no such benefit, or only some members receive one

criteria.note: Categorically eligible households are exempt from the income and resource tests. 7 CFR 273.2(j) and 273.8(a).

criteria.instructions: Is this household member aged 60 or older, or living with a disability?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is this person 60 or older, or living with a disability?
criteria.note: Drives three separate rules at once: no gross income test, a higher resource limit, and an uncapped shelter deduction. 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(i) and 273.9(d)(6)(ii).

criteria.instructions: Is the household's income from work, from benefits and other unearned sources, or both? Wages, salary, tips and self-employment are earned. Social Security, SSI, unemployment, pensions, child support received and disability payments are unearned.
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is that money from a job, or from benefits like Social Security?
criteria.note: Only earned income gets the 20% deduction, so this changes net income and the benefit figure. 7 CFR 273.9(d)(2).

criteria.instructions: Over what period is the stated income figure given? Choose the period the description actually uses, not the one that seems most likely.
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is that amount per week, per month, or per year?
criteria.note: A weekly figure read as monthly understates income more than fourfold. This is the criterion the adversarially phrased households are built to break.

criteria.instructions: Does the description state a rent, mortgage or housing cost the household pays?
criteria.askIfUnsure: How much do you pay for rent or mortgage each month?

criteria.true: yes, a housing cost is stated

criteria.instructions: Does the household pay for heating, cooling or utilities separately from its rent?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Do you pay for heating or electricity on top of your rent?

criteria.false: no, included in rent or not paid

criteria.note: Utilities count toward shelter costs, which raises the excess shelter deduction. 7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(ii).

criteria.instructions: Are all members of this household homeless, and not receiving free shelter throughout the month?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is everyone in your household without stable housing right now?
criteria.note: Takes a flat homeless shelter deduction instead of actual shelter costs. 7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(i).

criteria.instructions: Does the household pay for child care or dependent care in order to work, look for work, or attend training or school?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Do you pay for child care or care for an adult so that you can work or study?

criteria.instructions: Does any member pay legally obligated child support to someone outside the household?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Does anyone here pay court-ordered child support?

criteria.instructions: Does an elderly or disabled member have out-of-pocket medical costs above $35 a month?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Do you spend more than $35 a month on medical costs that insurance does not cover?
criteria.note: Available only to households with an elderly or disabled member. 7 CFR 273.9(d)(3).

criteria.instructions: Does the household hold countable resources — cash, bank accounts, stocks — above the limit? Retirement accounts and the home do not count.
criteria.askIfUnsure: Do you have more than a few thousand dollars in savings or a bank account?
criteria.note: 7 CFR 273.8(b). Most states have raised or removed this limit through broad-based categorical eligibility; this screening uses the federal floor.

criteria.instructions: Is this member aged 18 through 49 and enrolled at least half time in a college or other institution of higher education?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is this person in college at least half time?
criteria.note: Students meeting this description are ineligible unless an exemption applies. 7 CFR 273.5.

criteria.instructions: Does this student meet an exemption: working at least 20 hours a week, caring for a young child, receiving TANF, or in a state-approved work-study or training programme?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Does this student work 20 hours a week, or care for a young child?

criteria.instructions: What is this member's immigration status for SNAP purposes?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is this person a US citizen, or a lawful permanent resident?

criteria.qualified_noncitizen: lawful permanent resident or other qualified non-citizen

criteria.note: Ineligible members are excluded from the household size while their income may still count. 7 CFR 273.4.

criteria.instructions: Do the people described buy and prepare food together? People sharing an address but buying food separately are separate households.
criteria.askIfUnsure: Do you buy and cook food together with everyone you live with?
criteria.note: Defines who is in the household at all. 7 CFR 273.1(a).

criteria.instructions: Is any of the household's earned income from self-employment rather than wages?
criteria.askIfUnsure: Is any of that income from self-employment or your own business?
criteria.note: Self-employment income is counted net of business costs. 7 CFR 273.11(a).

verdict: categorical OR (gross_income_test AND net_income_test AND resource_test)
